title: Client unit tests get one fake DOM that can repaint (tidy first, before LIN-4246)
description:
## Goal

The browser code's unit tests have one small fake DOM with a home, good enough to repaint a page and see which nodes survive. Then a claim about what a repaint keeps can be witnessed in a unit test, not only in a slow end-to-end spec.

## Context

* `tests/unit/lin-4010-home-opened-task.test.js` runs `public/prompt-section.js` in a vm against a string-based fake. `querySelector` returns null, and there's no node identity, `replaceWith`, input value or focus, so it can't see whether a repaint kept a card.
* `tests/unit/lin-4242-waiting-merge.test.js` has its own hand-written parser and fake DOM.
* Client tests elsewhere stub `querySelector` selector by selector.
* "Shared test fakes with a home" has been named by five tickets (LIN-4177, LIN-4178, LIN-4241, LIN-4242, LIN-4048). Both Surveys of LIN-4246 named this gap as the reason its call-site witness would need a 180 s E2E spec.

## This step

A tidy, done first as its own task: one fake DOM, in a shared test-helper home, used by the two suites above, with the second fake deleted in the same change. It models what a repaint needs: node identity, `replaceWith` and `innerHTML`, an input's value, focus and `document.activeElement`. No production code changes.

**Not this ticket:** LIN-4246's witness (it comes next, on this fake); moving other client tests onto it; splitting `prompt-section.js`.

## Done when

* One fake DOM, with a home that other client tests can find, and the second copy gone.
* Both suites pass on it with the same test names and counts as before.
* Each thing the fake models has its own small test, so the fake itself can't silently pass.

## Report back

What the fake models, and what it deliberately doesn't. What moved. What had to learn about it.

## At merge (who else must learn about it)

* No production diff.
* CLAUDE.md names the home.
* The fake's tests run under `npm run test:unit`: show its file in the run.
* The report lists the remaining hand-written fakes by count, and every loosened regex.

## Survey (pruned at close-out)

The pre-work Surveys (10:15–10:17 at `29f14bf6`) were discharged by the landed work. Full text: the comment trail and the task snapshots.

## Implementation Plan

fits one session
plan-review due: no

**Implemented as approved** in [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2291](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2291>) (squash `d234b94a`): the shared fake DOM at `tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js` with its self-tests in `tests/unit/fake-dom.test.js`, the 4242 private fake deleted, `lin-4010` and `lin-4242` moved onto it (names and counts unchanged), one CLAUDE.md clause; no production diff. Deviations: the review's F1–F4 added `type` and `checked` to the fake, a `disabled` getter witness, and the `getClientRects` note (commit `6fee73d4`). Remaining hand-written fakes: LIN-4254. The full plan, Survey text and history are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4252 @ 29f14bf6e

**Why it will be hard: a real `querySelector` changes which code the 4010 suite runs.** Today `makeContainer().querySelector()` returns null, so every repaint in `public/prompt-section.js` takes its fallback. `paintState` (≈L1094), `paintRun` (L1142), `paintGo` and `paintLadder` (≈L1997, L2009) all do `if (slot) slot.outerHTML = …; else render()`, so the 43 tests only ever exercise a full `innerHTML` rewrite through `applyState`. Once the fake can find `[data-run-slot]`, the slot paths, `keepTypedQuestion`'s `fresh.replaceWith(oldQuestion)`, focus restore (`again.focus()`, `.type`, `setSelectionRange`), `container.parentElement` (`paintFoldCount`) and `e.target.closest('button, .swipe-reasoning-toggle')` all start running. "Same names and counts" could then mean the same titles over different code, so check that each test still proves its claim.

**The ticket's list of what to model misses things.** It names `replaceWith` and `innerHTML`, but the client repaints with an **`outerHTML` setter**. The selectors aren't simple ones either: descendant (`[data-run-slot] [data-testid=…]`), `:scope > a > b > c`, `button:not([disabled])` and comma lists in `closest`. 4242's `matches()` handles single compound selectors and throws on anything else. The selector engine is the biggest single piece of the fake, and it needs its own tests.

**The two suites read output in opposite ways.** 4010 asserts about 40 regexes against `c.innerHTML` *as a string*. 4242's `innerHTML` getter returns `''`, and its asserts walk nodes. The shared fake needs a serializer, and serializing faithfully breaks things. A browser writes the valueless `data-question-slot` as `data-question-slot=""`, which breaks the regex at L522 (`/data-question-slot>\s*<div/`). It also re-encodes entities (the parser decodes `"` and the like). Decide the serialization rule up front. Either it matches a browser and the few regexes that depend on it are loosened in place (names unchanged), or it echoes source. Echoing source would be a lie LIN-4246 builds on.

**There's a third copy.** `tests/unit/lin-3833-run-control.test.js:358` hand-builds an `outerHTML`-swapping slot with `focus()`→`doc.activeElement`, value and caret. It's the closest model of what LIN-4246 needs, and the ticket doesn't name it. About a dozen other suites carry their own `makeContainer`. Moving them is out of scope, but say so in the report so "one fake" isn't overclaimed.

**Smaller points:**
* `document.activeElement` is a plain field that 4242 sets directly. If `focus()` sets it instead, the fake has to own a per-world `document`.
* There are two helper homes. `tests/unit/helpers/` (already has `routing-fakes.js`) is the unit one. `tests/helpers.js` is the E2E selector seam per CLAUDE.md.
* No DOM library is installed (no jsdom, linkedom or happy-dom), so hand-rolled is the house precedent.

**The deeper issue:** prompt-section's `container.querySelector ? … : null` guards and `else render()` fallbacks read as if they were written for the string fakes. The client's partial-repaint paths have had no unit witness at all, not only the LIN-4246 one.

**What I'd do first:** in the 4010 sandbox, swap `makeContainer` for a recording Proxy. Run the 43 tests and log every DOM member and selector prompt-section touches once the slots can be found. That log is the fake's spec and its list of self-tests. Then settle serialization before moving 4242. Baseline at this commit: 4010 = 43/43, 4242-merge = 13/13.

## Survey global: LIN-4252 @ 29f14bf6e

**Where it lands.** In `tests/unit`, where 96 suites run `public/*.js` in a vm. There are three homes for shared fakes already: `tests/unit/helpers/` (routing-fakes.js), `tests/unit/lib/` (proxy-fake-deps.js, whose header explains why shared code must not live in a `.test.js`), and `tests/helpers/`. CLAUDE.md names none of the unit ones. 19 suites each hand-write a `makeContainer`, and several (prompt-section-preserve, -go, lin-3833, lin-4016) stub `querySelector(sel)` selector by selector. Copies are still multiplying: LIN-4242 added a full parser today. This fixes a widening gap.

**What the obvious way gets wrong.**
1. **The two fakes aren't peers.** lin-4242's runs `question-cards.js`, not prompt-section. It already has node identity, a parser, `.value` and an assignable `activeElement`, so lifting it out is the obvious move. It has two traps: its `innerHTML` getter returns `''`, and `matches()` throws on anything but one compound selector.
2. **lin-4010 is the hard migration.** Its 45 tests assert regexes over `c.innerHTML` as a string (for example `class="btn btn--primary opened-task-write" data-testid="opened-task-write"`). On a real tree the getter has to *serialize* faithfully (attribute order, quoting, entities). If it doesn't, the tests pass only by loosening their regexes: same names and counts, weaker witness. Today its `querySelector` returns null, so prompt-section skips all 44 `querySelector` paths. Once nodes come back, the code meets `[data-run-slot] [data-testid="…"]`, `:scope > … > …`, `:not([disabled])`, comma lists and `closest` (7 uses).
3. **The model list leaves out prompt-section's main repaint.** That is the `slot.outerHTML = …` setter (lines 1095, 1120, 1149, 1997, 2009). `replaceWith` appears once (993, `keepTypedQuestion`), and that same line compares `oldQuestion.innerHTML === fresh.innerHTML`. With lin-4242's `''` getter the comparison is always true, so the card is always kept and LIN-4246's witness would pass silently. LIN-4246 also needs `QuestionCards` in the same sandbox. If this fake lacks the outerHTML setter, a real serializer, combinators and `closest`, LIN-4246 ends up growing it inside its own witness change.
4. **Where its tests live matters.** `test:unit` globs only `tests/unit/*.test.js`. A test next to the helper in a subfolder would never run, and nothing would notice. The hermetic file count is derived from that top level, so a top-level test needs no registration.

**Better, at this task's cost.** Put the fake in `tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`, with tests at `tests/unit/fake-dom.test.js`. Model the outerHTML setter, a faithful `innerHTML`/`outerHTML` serializer, descendant and child combinators, `closest`, and focus/`activeElement`. Unsupported selectors should **throw**, as lin-4242's do, so gaps are loud. Give each capability a test, including "changed markup compares unequal". Keep lin-4010's `click`/`key` shims as a thin layer in that suite. Add one line to CLAUDE.md's Unit Testing section naming the home, which is what makes it findable.

**Better still, not this task's.** Moving the other 17 `makeContainer` copies. Removing prompt-section's `container.querySelector ? … : null` guards, which exist so production code tolerates null-returning fakes. Settling on one of the three helper homes. Splitting the 2,885-line prompt-section.js.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve. The premise holds, the scope matches what was asked, and the order fits. Four notes for the builder. Note 1 will show up as red tests in step 3. Notes 2 and 3 would pass silently and leave the fake lying, so they need deliberate attention.

**What I checked, at `29f14bf6` (still main; nothing has landed on these files since the ticket was created)**
- Baseline: `node --test` on the two suites gives 56/56 (43 + 13).
- `test:unit` globs only top-level `tests/unit/*.test.js`. The hermetic runner derives its expected count from `readdirSync(tests/unit)` (`scripts/assert-unit-suite-hermetic.mjs:188`), so a top-level `fake-dom.test.js` needs no registration. No code-shape or census gate looks at `tests/unit/helpers/`.
- `CLAUDE.md` is 110 lines and 11,482 bytes, against caps of 110 / 12,000. Appending to the end of the paragraph at L58 fits.
- The 4242 fake has the traps the plan describes: `innerHTML` getter returns `''`, `matches()` takes one compound selector, text is a single `_text` string. `document.activeElement` is assigned directly (L253), so the setter is needed.
- The repaint paths and line numbers are right: `slot.outerHTML` at L1095/1120/1149/1997/2009, `replaceWith` at L993 together with the `innerHTML ===` comparison, focus restore at L1144–1158, `parentElement` at L1108.
- prompt-section's selector literals all fall inside the planned engine: attribute and class selectors, a descendant selector, `:scope > a > b > c`, `button:not([disabled])`, and comma lists in `closest` (including `MARKDOWN_SINK`). The renderers emit no SVG, no `/>`, and only the entities `& < > "` (plus `'` from `escapeHtml`).

**Notes (act on these while building; none of them changes the plan's shape)**

1. **The 4010 click and key shims cannot keep passing stub targets.** The plan says they call the listeners "with the stub `{ target: btn }` they build today". That breaks once `contains` is real. `handleClick` returns early on `!container.contains(btn)` (prompt-section L2455), and `onRunKeydown` does the same on `!container.contains(e.target)` (L1797). The key shim today calls `fn(target)`, so `e.target` is `undefined`. Every test driven through `c.click` or `c.key` (8 calls) will then fail, or silently stop testing anything. Fix it in the shims:
   - `click(dataset)` finds the real control, e.g. `c.querySelector('[data-action="change-run"]')`. If the control isn't there it throws, naming it. It then passes that node as `target`.
   - `key(k)` passes `{ key: k, target: <a node inside c>, preventDefault() {} }`.
   - Don't override `contains`, and don't let it accept non-nodes. That would bring back the lie the ticket is removing.
   - If a click goes red because its button isn't actually rendered, that is a finding under the plan's own rule. This shim change is a test fix, not a loosening. List it in the report under "what had to learn about it".

2. **Reflect the properties the code reads, or the fake lies about controls.** Behaviour 5 covers `value` and the caret, but the code also reads and writes these properties, which a browser keeps in sync with attributes:
   - `disabled`: prompt-section L2459, L2635, L2639, L2705; question-cards ×10.
   - `checked`: L2729, L2737.
   - `type`: L1156. An `<input>` with no `type` attribute reads `'text'`. question-cards L160 sets it.

   With plain own properties:
   - a parsed `<button disabled>` reads `btn.disabled === undefined`, so a click goes through where a browser would refuse it;
   - `again.type === 'text'` is false for a default input, so the caret restore is skipped without any sign;
   - `btn.disabled = true` neither serializes nor affects `:not([disabled])`.

   Model these as getters and setters backed by the attributes, and give each one a test. One example: "`btn.disabled = true` serializes `disabled=\"\"` and is excluded by `button:not([disabled])`". A recording Proxy on the container won't log these, because they are read on descendants. Add them to the step-1 grep explicitly.

3. **The focus-removal rule needs the 4010 container to be attached.** If "a replaced or removed control is no longer `activeElement`" is implemented through `isConnected`, a control inside 4010's container, which today has no parent, would always read as disconnected. `document.activeElement` would then always be `null`, and the focus-restore path (L1144) would never be exercised, which is the very path LIN-4246 needs. Fix: mount the 4010 container under the world's root or body, and use that world's `document` as the sandbox `document`, adding `body.appendChild`/`removeChild` on top. Add a fake-dom test that a focused control in an attached subtree stays `activeElement` across an unrelated repaint.

4. **The plan is wrong that the browser throws on an `outerHTML` set with no parent.** Per the spec's `outerHTML` setter, a null parent means the set silently does nothing. The browser throws `NoModificationAllowedError` only when the parent is a Document. Throwing anyway is a reasonable choice for the fake's job of refusing to lie, but name it in the helper's header and in the test title as a deliberate strictness beyond the browser, not as matching it. Or make it a no-op like the browser. Either way, don't call it browser behaviour.

**Smaller points**
- Expect the `hidden` regexes at L608/L610 to stay green: `[^>]*hidden` still matches `hidden=""`. L522 is the one certain loosening. Loosen only what actually goes red, as the plan already says.
- `keepFocusInDrawer` (L1808) calls `getClientRects()`, but only on Tab, and no test presses Tab. Leave it unmodelled and say in the report that it is touched but never reached. LIN-4246 can add it if it needs it.
- 4010 doesn't load `QuestionCards`, so `keepTypedQuestion`'s `keepsReaderPlace` branch is false there. Only the `innerHTML ===` half of L993 runs in 4010, so "changed markup compares unequal" is the fake-dom test that guards it.

The plan goes to `implementation` with these notes.

LIN-4252 done, PR ready for review: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2291

- Commit: 04b75fda on feat/lin-4252-shared-fake-dom (four ordered commits, no production diff).
- Fake: tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js, self-tests in tests/unit/fake-dom.test.js (42 pass). Mutation checks turn them red.
- lin-4242-waiting-merge moved (private fake deleted), 13/13. lin-4010-home-opened-task moved, 43/43. Names unchanged.
- One regex loosened: the question-slot regex now accepts data-question-slot="". Renaming the attribute turns it red. The Escape test got the preview its Change button needs (its old click hit nothing drawn).
- npm run test:unit: 23,331 pass, 0 fail. test:hermetic:keyed: PASS. CI success on PR #2291.
- Decision for review: outerHTML= on a parentless node is a no-op (DOM Parsing spec), not a throw.
- Remaining hand-written fakes: 18 files. Follow-up: LIN-4254.

## Review — LIN-4252

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2291, head `04b75fdac582427ad4aedabda2dfcd39799d6805` (base `40557e9f`, current main).

CI: green on head `04b75fda` (Unit tests, E2E 1–4/4, Secret scan, CI success). `.github/workflows/test.yml` exists, so the ordinary gate applies.

### What I checked
- **Scope matches the plan.** The diff touches only `CLAUDE.md`, `tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`, `tests/unit/fake-dom.test.js`, and the two named suites. There is no production diff. The 4242 private `FakeNode`/parser is deleted. `fake-dom.test.js` sits at the top level, so the `test:unit` glob picks it up. The CLAUDE.md clause is appended to the Unit Testing paragraph.
- **Same names and counts.** I re-ran the three files locally: 98/98 (42 + 43 + 13). Diffing the `test(`/`describe(` titles against main shows no change in either suite.
- **Regression check.** Nothing has landed on these files since the ticket was created. The recent history (LIN-4242, 4168, 4107, 4106…) shows nothing reverted that this change re-applies.
- **Settled decisions.** `outerHTML =` on a parentless node is a no-op, which matches the brief, and the test title names the spec, not a throw. The click shim finds the real button and throws if it isn't drawn. The key shim targets `document.activeElement`. `contains` is not overridden. The container is mounted under the world's body (plan-review note 3).
- **Loosened regexes.** Only L522 was loosened, to `data-question-slot(?:="")?`. That matches what the plan predicted.
- **Remaining fakes.** The grep (`makeContainer|class FakeNode|parseHtml`, excluding 4010) counts 18. The follow-up LIN-4254 exists (Backlog).
- **No rulings** exist on LIN-4252, so nothing is re-raised here.

### Mutation checks (each reverted; the tree is clean)
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `paintRun`: drop `again.focus()` | 1 red (Escape test) ✔ |
| fake `:not` always true | 1 red ✔ |
| fake `:scope` matches anything | 1 red ✔ |
| fake `>` treated as descendant | 2 red ✔ |
| fake `value` setter ignored | 4 red ✔ |
| **fake `get disabled()` always `false`** | **0 red ✘** |
| **`paintRun`: drop the typed-value/caret restore (`if (typed && again.type === 'text')` → `if (false)`)** | **0 red ✘** |

### Findings
1. **`type` is not modelled, and nothing says so** (inside: brief "form/control state … including `value`, `disabled`, `checked`, `type`", and plan-review note 2). `again.type` reads `undefined` on the fake, so prompt-section L1156's restore of typed value and caret can never run under this fake. It is skipped without any sign. That is the second mutation that survived. The PR's "not modelled" list leaves `type` out. `question-cards.js:160` (`retryBtn.type = 'button'`) also sets a plain own property, which never serializes.
2. **`checked` is listed as "deliberately not modelled"**, but the brief and plan-review note 2 (prompt-section L2729, L2737) asked for it. Its absence is silent in the same way: `el.checked === true` is always false.
3. **The `disabled` getter has no witness.** "hidden and disabled reflect their attributes" exercises only the setter. Plan-review note 2's own example, a parsed `<button disabled>` reading `.disabled === true`, is untested, so the fake could lie about it and stay green (the first mutation that survived).
4. Report note only: `keepFocusInDrawer` (L1808) calls `getClientRects()`, which the fake doesn't model. It is reached only on Tab, and no test presses Tab. Plan review asked for this to be stated in the report, and the PR doesn't state it.

### Fixes for close-out to make (in `tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js` and `tests/unit/fake-dom.test.js`)
- **F1 `type`.** Add a `FakeElement` getter and setter. For `<input>`, the getter returns the lowercased `type` attribute, or `'text'` when the attribute is absent. For `<button>`, it returns the attribute or `'submit'`. For other elements, it returns the attribute or `''`. The setter does `setAttribute('type', v)`. Add the test "an input with no type attribute reads type 'text', and setting type reflects to the attribute" (for example, `b.type = 'button'` serializes `type="button"`).
- **F2 `checked`.** On `<input>`, the value starts from `hasAttribute('checked')`. Once set, it is independent and not serialized, the same pattern as `value`. Add a test that checks both halves. Then remove `checked` from the header's "not modelled" list and the PR body.
- **F3 `disabled` getter.** Extend the reflect test to parse `<button disabled>` and assert `.disabled === true`, and to assert that after `b.disabled = true` the button is excluded by `button:not([disabled])`.
- **F4 Report.** Add the `getClientRects`/Tab note to the PR body, and correct the "not modelled" list.
- Then re-run the three suites, `npm run test:unit`, and `claude-md-line-budget`, and confirm that the F1 test goes red when the `type` getter is removed and the F3 test goes red when the `disabled` getter returns `false`.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (brief, form/control state): F1–F3 above. The fake skips the typed-value restore and the `checked`/`disabled` reads, and stays green while doing it. **Before the merge:** make F1–F3. The distinguishing condition is that the `disabled` getter mutation and a `type` getter removal each turn a `fake-dom.test.js` test red.
- **Outside** (LIN-4246's witness, not this ticket's): no 4010 test drives the L1155–1158 typed-value/caret restore. Dropping it leaves 98/98 green. After F1 the fake can witness it, and LIN-4246 is the ticket that adds that witness. It is listed here so nobody reads "repaint paths now run" as "the typed restore is tested". No new ticket is needed.
- **Outside**: the 18 remaining hand-written fakes are already routed to LIN-4254. Discharged by that follow-up.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The shared fake, the moves, the deletion and the shims are sound, and CI is green on `04b75fda`. Before merge, close-out must make the three small form-control fixes F1–F3 (with their mutation checks) and the report correction F4.

## Close-out — LIN-4252

**Merged:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2291, squash commit `d234b94a` on main, pinned with `--match-head-commit 6fee73d4`. Test-only change (shared fake DOM at `tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`, its self-tests, the two migrated suites, one CLAUDE.md clause), no production diff, so no deploy and no post-deploy step.

**Authority:** review Approve (comment on head `04b75fda`) with a ledger, conditional on F1–F4.

### Changes I made after the approval (commit `6fee73d4`)
- **F1** (review finding 1) `type` getter/setter on the fake: input `text`, button `submit`, other `''`, setter reflects to the attribute. New test "an input with no type attribute reads type 'text'…".
- **F2** (finding 2) `checked` on inputs: starts from the attribute, then independent and unserialized. New test; removed from the "not modelled" list.
- **F3** (finding 3) `disabled` getter witness: parsed `<button disabled>` reads true, `button:not([disabled])` excludes a button after `disabled = true`.
- **F4** (finding 4) header and PR body: `getClientRects`/Tab path (`keepFocusInDrawer`) listed as not modelled; the lists and counts corrected.

### Ledger
- **Inside, F1–F3: done, with the distinguishing mutation checks the review named** (each reverted afterwards): `disabled` getter forced `false` → 1 red (`hidden and disabled reflect…`); `type` getter removed → 1 red (the F1 test); `checked` ignoring its attribute → 1 red (the F2 test).
- **Outside, 4010 typed-value/caret restore (L1155–1158) has no test:** the fake can now witness it (`type` reads `text`); LIN-4246 adds that witness. Nothing is claimed here beyond that. No new ticket, per review.
- **Outside, 18 remaining hand-written fakes:** LIN-4254 (already filed). I gave it priority Low (lowest: test-only, no production risk), label Improvement (nearest catalog fit; no test-infra label exists), and linked it `related` to LIN-4252.
- No named monitor or rollback was required by the review. No rulings exist on LIN-4252.

### CI
CI applies (`.github/workflows/test.yml`). Green on the exact merged head `6fee73d4`: Unit tests, E2E 1–4/4, Secret scan, CI success. Locally on that head: `fake-dom` + 4010 + 4242 = 100/100 (98 + 2 new), `claude-md-line-budget` 2/2, `npm run test:unit` 23,333 pass / 0 fail. After the merge, the same three suites on main at `d234b94a`: 100/100. Not proven: a clean-environment run outside CI.

### Housekeeping
Description archived (snapshot) and pruned; related tickets checked (LIN-4246 stays open and is the next step on this fake).

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why it was difficult.** The fake itself wasn't hard: a tree, a parser, a serializer, a small selector engine. The work bound in the lin-4010 harness. The old stub's `querySelector` returned null and `contains` returned true, so every test ran `prompt-section.js`'s `else render()` fallback and every click landed. Two things had to give. First, the container and the sandbox's `document` had to share one world, but tests built them in separate calls; `loadClient` now returns a `makeContainer` bound to its own world. Second, the shims had to target real nodes, which surfaced the Escape test clicking a Change button that was never drawn because the test supplied no preview. Moderate: mostly care and volume.

**2. What I'd have done first.** Checked the browser's `outerHTML` behaviour on a parentless node before writing the helper, rather than meeting the contradiction mid-build. I'd also have run the recording-Proxy probe the plan suggested; I used a static grep instead, which was enough here, but the probe would have found the preview-dependent Change button before the suite went red.

**3. What I'd tidy.** `container.click = …` puts own properties on a fake element and shadows a method name a browser element has; a separate `{ el, click, key }` shim would be cleaner. The selector cache is an unbounded module-level Map. The caret starting at the end of the value is a modelled guess, marked in the header but not checked against a browser. One of my own mutation checks (focus fixup) first survived because `isConnected` masked it; I added a re-insertion test.

**4. What the ticket would have been.** If the repaint decisions in `prompt-section.js` (keep the typed question, restore focus) were functions from old and new markup to a decision, with a small apply step, LIN-4246's witness would need no DOM. The ticket would then have been "pull `keepTypedQuestion`'s decision out and test it", not "build a fake browser".

**5. What the ticket got wrong.** "`outerHTML =` on a parentless node throws, as a browser does": the DOM Parsing spec says it's a no-op, which I followed. The predicted regex breaks (`hidden`, `'`) didn't happen; only the slot regex did. The plan's shims "with the stub `{ target: btn }`" couldn't survive a real `contains`. The 18-file count was right.

**6. What it left behind.** A third helper home in `tests/unit/helpers/` beside `routing-fakes.js` and `frozen-resolvers-*.js`, still unsettled. Two ways to fake a DOM, until LIN-4254 moves the other 18 files. The CLAUDE.md line names the home, but nothing enforces it. The `container.querySelector ? … : null` guards are now dead for the moved suites but still in production. Simpler: 4242 lost about 160 lines, and 4010's Escape test now also witnesses focus restore.

**7. Did the larger scope pay?** Yes, for moving 4010. Every finding came from running real repaint paths under it: the undrawn button, the focus-restore witness, and nine tests that now go red if the run-block repaint stops. The helper alone would have been verified only against itself. The CLAUDE.md line and the commit order were cheap. I'd draw the line where the ticket did: lin-3833's hand-built slot needs its own suite's container moved first, so it belongs with the other 18.
